title: Interior Music
label: Bang & Olufsen
overview:
A promotional release of 2001 for Bang & Olufsen, the Danish audio maker, which commissioned Jarre to write background music for one of its stores. MusicBrainz lists it as a French promotion release of two tracks, and a fan site reports a run of only 1,000 copies and credits Jarre as producer. The same site notes that the sleeve says the music would be part of a new album, which never happened. No other credits or equipment are documented in the sources found.

The disc holds two pieces of almost the same length. "Bonjour-Hello" combines vocal snippets, nature sounds and short spoken sentences in French, Danish and English; "Whispers of Life" is its instrumental version. The timeline below is a rough guide taken from measuring the rip, not from a full listen: both pieces start very quietly, rise in sudden surges and drops, and keep to the same plan.

tracks.title: Bonjour-Hello
tracks.role: Album role: The first of the two long pieces, the version with voices, nature sounds and spoken sentences in three languages.

events.description: A very quiet, sparse opening with almost no low end.
events.detail: A fan site describes the track as vocal snippets with nature sounds and short spoken sentences in French, Danish and English, for example "You look handsome"; it did not give times for them.

events.description: The low end and the middle range come in and the level rises sharply for the first time.
A deep low end enters and the level jumps to the first loud passage of the track.
The level falls to near silence for a few seconds, then the low end returns at 3:05.
The low end swells suddenly, the largest change in this stretch of the piece.
A sudden low-end swell leads into a louder passage at about 7:15.
One of the louder passages of the piece, lasting under a minute.
Another loud stretch, followed by a quieter passage from about 17:00.
The level drops away and the piece fades to silence.

tracks.title: Whispers of Life
tracks.role: Album role: The second long piece, the instrumental version of "Bonjour-Hello".

events.description: A very quiet, sparse opening like that of the first track.
events.detail: A fan site states that this track is the instrumental version of "Bonjour-Hello".

events.description: The low end comes in and the level rises sharply, at the same point as in the first track.
The level falls to near silence, and the low end returns at 3:06.
The low end comes back strongly after the drop.
A large step up in level and low end begins the next section.
The loudest passage of the album, a short stretch in which the level rises above anything else on the disc.
A short, sharp rise in level that falls back within seconds.
Another loud stretch, in the same place as in the first track.
